boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named public destinations along Marion corridors, each paired with one specific, city-documented reason to leave campus.

cards.title: Shoot Hoops Near the Grocery Run
cards.subtitle: 28th Street at Terrace Street
cards.notes: Pair an errand on the 28th Street corridor with time on the park’s playground or basketball court before its posted closing time.
cards.short_summary: A compact recreation stop on the 28th Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marion identifies 28th Street Park at 28th and Terrace Street and documents a playground, basketball court, and daily hours of 7 a.m.–9 p.m.
cards.source_title: Parks & Attractions | City of Marion Parks & Recreation Department
cards.access_notes: City-posted hours are 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; outdoor amenities may be weather-dependent.

cards.title: Find a Full-Size Soccer Stop
cards.subtitle: State Road 18 at Pennsylvania Street
cards.notes: Use the State Road 18 corridor stop for soccer practice or a scheduled match, and do not assume field lighting is available otherwise.
cards.short_summary: Nineteen acres of soccer space beside State Road 18.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marion places Ballard Field Soccer Complex at State Road 18 and Pennsylvania Street and documents three soccer fields, practice space, and event restrooms.
cards.source_title: Parks & Attractions | City of Marion Parks & Recreation Department
cards.access_notes: City-posted hours are 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; lighting is available for scheduled games.

cards.title: Trade a Screen for a Little Library
cards.subtitle: 6th Street at E Street
cards.notes: Turn off the 6th Street corridor to browse the miniature free library, then use the shelter or playground for an outdoor break.
cards.short_summary: Books and play space meet at a two-acre neighborhood park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marion locates Barnes Park at 6th and E Street and documents a shelter, playground, and miniature free library on its two acres.
cards.source_title: Parks & Attractions | City of Marion Parks & Recreation Department
cards.access_notes: City-posted hours are 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; the listed amenities are outdoors.

cards.title: Try the Outdoor Fitness Studio
cards.subtitle: North Washington Street at Charles Street
cards.notes: Follow North Washington Street to the marked fitness station; consult its posted guidance or companion app before starting a circuit.
cards.short_summary: A three-acre river-area park built around movement.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marion places Charles Mill Park at North Washington and Charles streets and documents a walking path, basketball court, library, and outdoor Fitness Court Studio.
cards.source_title: Parks & Attractions | City of Marion Parks & Recreation Department
cards.access_notes: City-posted hours are 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; follow instructions displayed on the outdoor fitness equipment.

cards.title: Make a Small Playground Detour
cards.subtitle: West 2nd Street at Butler Street
cards.notes: Take the West 2nd Street corridor to this one-acre park when a simple playground stop fits better than a long outing.
cards.short_summary: A focused play-space detour off West 2nd Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marion locates Franklin Park at West 2nd and Butler streets and describes a one-acre green space with a mulched playground area.
cards.source_title: Parks & Attractions | City of Marion Parks & Recreation Department
cards.access_notes: City-posted hours are 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; the playground is an outdoor facility.

cards.title: Join the Cardinal Greenway
cards.subtitle: 14th Street at Valley Avenue
cards.notes: Enter from the 14th Street corridor for a walk, skate, or bike connection to the adjacent Cardinal Greenway; yield to other trail users.
cards.short_summary: Nine acres with a direct reason to continue onto the greenway.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marion places Hogin Park at 14th Street and Valley Avenue and documents a walking path, skate park, courts, seating, and adjacent Cardinal Greenway access.
cards.source_title: Parks & Attractions | City of Marion Parks & Recreation Department
cards.access_notes: City-posted hours are 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; bring appropriate safety equipment for biking or skating.

cards.title: Choose a Disc-Golf Loop
cards.subtitle: River Road at Quarry Road
cards.notes: Head along the River Road corridor with discs or court gear; choose one documented activity instead of trying to cover all 110 acres.
cards.short_summary: Marion’s large north-side park offers a full recreation menu.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marion places Matter Park at River and Quarry roads and documents disc golf, tennis, pickleball, playgrounds, shelters, gardens, and a fishing pond.
cards.source_title: Parks & Attractions | City of Marion Parks & Recreation Department
cards.access_notes: City-posted hours are 7 a.m.–11 p.m.; the pond is designated for catch-and-release fishing.

cards.title: Walk Toward Charles Mill Park
cards.subtitle: Boots Street at Massey Street
cards.notes: Start on the Boots Street corridor and use the documented walking-path connection toward Charles Mill Park for a longer outing.
cards.short_summary: A three-acre park that extends into a connected walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marion places North Boots Street Park at Massey and Boots streets and documents a shelter, playground, and walking path connecting to Charles Mill Park.
cards.source_title: Parks & Attractions | City of Marion Parks & Recreation Department
cards.access_notes: City-posted hours are 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; remain on the designated walking connection.

cards.title: Cool Off in the Wave Pool
cards.subtitle: South Adams Street near 26th Street
cards.notes: Check the seasonal schedule before taking the South Adams Street corridor; lifeguards staff the city’s slides, lazy river, and wave pool.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal, family-oriented water-park stop on South Adams Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marion lists Splash House at 2601 South Adams Street and documents a lazy river, slides, children’s area, wave pool, concessions, and lifeguards.
cards.source_title: Parks & Attractions | City of Marion Parks & Recreation Department
cards.access_notes: The city lists seasonal hours of 11 a.m.–6 p.m., Tuesday–Sunday; verify operating dates before traveling.

cards.title: Pick a Playground for a Picnic
cards.subtitle: 7th Street at Michigan Avenue
cards.notes: Turn from the 7th Street corridor with a packed snack and choose among the park’s playground areas and picnic seating.
cards.short_summary: A west-side play stop with room for a simple picnic.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marion locates West Point Park at 7th Street and Michigan Avenue and documents several playground areas and picnic seating on one acre.
cards.source_title: Parks & Attractions | City of Marion Parks & Recreation Department
cards.access_notes: City-posted hours are 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; playground and picnic facilities are outdoors.

warnings: Coordinates were left null because exact destination coordinates were not independently verified.
The City of Marion consolidates current locations, amenities, and hours for all ten destinations on one official page.
